result.question: Deep research for a decision study (final report in Arabic): A merchant sells women's clothing, kids' clothing, and women's watches via Meta Click-to-WhatsApp ads with cash-on-delivery in Palestine/Middle East, building an automated system (Marketing API bulk ad generation from catalog variants, WhatsApp Cloud API bot, CAPI with ctwa_clid attribution). Decision to research: should WATCHES be separated from CLOTHING, and at which level — Business Manager, Pixel/Dataset, Catalog, Campaigns, Bot flows? Research axes: (1) Meta catalog spec for watches: variant fields beyond size/color (material, pattern, custom labels), how to model dial color × band color/material × case diameter, item_group_id rules, google_product_category for watches; (2) One multi-category catalog vs separate catalogs: official Meta guidance, Product Sets as the segmentation tool, effects on Advantage+ Catalog Ads, catalog limits, real advertiser experiences (r/FacebookAds, agency blogs); (3) Shared vs separate Pixel/Dataset: effect of mixing clothing+watch purchase signals on algorithm learning and Lookalikes; (4) Campaign structure: separate campaigns per product line, auction overlap between women's-clothing and women's-watch audiences, small budget ($20-30/day) sequencing, when to launch the watches campaign; (5) Trademark/counterfeit risk specifically for watches on Meta: commerce policies, Brand Rights Protection program, account bans from branded watch ads, safe rules for private-label/no-logo watches; (6) WhatsApp bot flow differences for watches (no size question; dial/band choice), WhatsApp catalog messages (Single/Multi-Product Messages) across categories; (7) Benchmarks: watches/jewelry/accessories vs apparel on Meta (CPC, CTR, CVR, ROAS, AOV), COD delivery-refusal rates for watches vs clothing in Arab markets; (8) Technical examples on GitHub: Marketing API scripts for multi-category catalogs, real watch product feed structures. Prioritize official Meta developer/business docs, then agencies/forums/GitHub. Output should support a clear per-level separate-vs-merge verdict.

confirmed.claim: Meta catalog variant attributes are category-dependent and go beyond size and color: they can include material, pattern, gender, and additional attributes such as fit, edition or flavor — meaning a watch can be varianted on material (band/case material) and pattern/color (dial), not just apparel-style size/color.
confirmed.quote: Variant attributes depend on your item's category, but can include size, color, material, pattern, gender or additional attributes such as fit, edition or flavor.

confirmed.claim: Variants are grouped by giving every variant item the same value in the item_group_id field; each variant is otherwise a separate catalog item with its own unique id.
confirmed.quote: Enter the same group ID in this field for all variants of the same product to indicate they're part of a group.

confirmed.claim: Meta's Advantage+ catalog ads natively support showing groups of items (categories) instead of individual products, meaning a single catalog containing both clothing and watches can be segmented at the ad level without splitting into separate catalogs.
confirmed.quote: Rather than showing individual items, you can segment the items in your ads by specific categories (for example, swimwear) or brands (for example, Facebook).

unverified.claim: Category segmentation within one catalog is driven by three catalog feed fields — brand, product_type, or google_product_category — so correctly populating google_product_category/product_type for watches vs. apparel enables in-catalog separation.

Meta's Advertising Standards prohibit ads containing any content that violates a third party's intellectual property rights, including both copyright and trademark, making trademark infringement in watch ads a policy violation at the ad level.

Meta defines counterfeit goods as products that copy a company's trademark (name or logo) AND/OR the distinctive features of its products — meaning a watch with no logo can still be counterfeit under this policy if it imitates a genuine product's distinctive design.
The prohibition explicitly extends beyond exact counterfeits to knockoffs and replicas of another company's products, which covers 'replica' or 'homage' watches commonly sold in COD dropshipping.
Meta/Facebook strongly recommends that an advertiser use a single product catalog for all advertising needs (both ads and Shops), rather than splitting product lines into multiple catalogs.

Catalog-level performance learnings accumulate with spend on a specific catalog, and creating a new/separate catalog resets that learning: the new catalog inherits none of the optimization data from past events on the old catalog.

Product Sets (created in Commerce Manager) are the intended mechanism for segmenting a single catalog by category so you can run targeted ads per product group (e.g., watches vs. clothing) without fragmenting catalog learnings across multiple catalogs.

When deciding campaign structure, advertisers should default to consolidating rather than fragmenting into new campaigns, because consolidation concentrates a finite budget on a single goal and reduces complexity — directly relevant to whether the merchant should split watches into a separate campaign on a $20-30/day budget.

Running multiple ad sets or campaigns that can reach the same people causes auction overlap, where the advertiser competes against themself in Meta's ad auction, driving up costs or causing under-delivery — the key mechanism to weigh when separating women's-watch campaigns from women's-clothing campaigns targeting overlapping audiences.
In most cases a single ad set per campaign is sufficient, and advertisers no longer need separate ad sets for broad, lookalike, detailed-targeting, demographic, or remarketing segmentation.

When variants are set up correctly, Meta shows only one variant per item group in ads and shops instead of several near-duplicate listings — relevant to whether dial-color × band-material combinations should be modeled as one item group (one ad slot) or separate products (multiple ad slots).
Correct variant setup improves discovery: when a customer clicks an item in an ad or shop, they may see the other variants (colors, sizes, patterns, materials) on its product page.

Each category in an Advantage+ catalog ad can have its own custom image, headline, and destination URL, allowing differentiated creative/messaging for a watches category vs. clothing categories without separate campaigns or catalogs.

Category definitions created in Ads Manager are persisted and reusable across campaigns, and edits to categories propagate back to the catalog itself, reducing the operational overhead of managing a single multi-category catalog.

Category ads are personalized: Meta selects which categories a given customer sees based on their interests and purchase intent, so mixed-category catalogs still deliver interest-matched groupings (e.g., watches shown to watch-intenders).

Ads are prohibited if they are likely to confuse people about the source, sponsorship or affiliation of goods — so watch ads implying a brand association (styling, brand-adjacent naming) violate policy even without selling a fake.

Enforcement is two-channel: ads can be rejected or removed either because a rights holder reports them (e.g., via Brand Rights Protection) or proactively when Meta detects signs of infringement, so a private-label watch seller can be enforced against without any complaint being filed.

The main drawback of the single-catalog approach is creative, not delivery: you cannot A/B test catalog creatives within one catalog, and default catalog ads all look alike (plain product images on white backgrounds).

Supplementary feeds allow an advertiser to modify catalog content (e.g., swap product images per collection) while keeping the existing catalog and its campaign learnings intact, offering another alternative to creating separate catalogs.

Adding targeting or placement restrictions limits the options available to Meta's delivery algorithm and is usually counterproductive, since the algorithm should be allowed to find converters on its own (e.g., via Advantage+ Audience when optimizing for conversions).

The historical rationale for creating many campaigns — asserting manual control over testing and delivery — is largely obsolete in Meta's current automation-driven system, so structural separation should only be done for genuinely different goals, not for perceived control.

Commerce Manager exposes variant grouping for verification: the Catalog > Items tab shows the number of variants per item in a Variants column, and items with two or more variants can be expanded to view the whole group — usable as a QA check for an automated feed that mixes clothing and watch item groups.
